1.name: Spellcasting
1.notes:
You have learned to cast spells as a student of arcane magic.

Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice (Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended). Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Wizard cantrip of your choice. At Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn one additional Wizard cantrip, as shown in the class table.

Spellbook. Your studies culminated in the creation of your spellbook. It is a Tiny object (3 pounds, 100 pages) that can be read only by you or by someone casting Identify. You determine its appearance and materials.
The book contains the level 1+ Wizard spells you know. It begins with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice (Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended).
Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, you add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table.

Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare a list of Wizard spells of level 1+ that you can cast. To start, choose four spells from your spellbook. Each prepared spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
The number of prepared spells increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table; whenever that number increases, you choose additional spells from your spellbook to match the new total.
If another Wizard feature gives you spells that are always prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare, but they count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of them with other spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook. The spells you gain when leveling reflect your ongoing research, but you can also add spells you find:
• Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it is of a level you can prepare and you have the time and resources. Copying takes 2 hours and 50 GP per spell level. Once copied, you can prepare the spell like any other in your book.
• Copying the Book. You can copy spells from your spellbook into another book. This is faster because you already know the spells: it takes 1 hour and 10 GP per spell level.
• Replacing a Lost Book. If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same process to transcribe the Wizard spells you currently have prepared into a new book. Filling out the remainder of the new spellbook requires you to find additional spells. Many wizards keep a backup spellbook for this reason.

1.name: Ritual Adept
1.notes: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if the spell has the Ritual tag and is in your spellbook. You need not have the spell prepared, but you must read from your spellbook when casting it as a Ritual.

1.name: Arcane Recovery
1.notes:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can recover expended spell slots with a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the recovered slots can be level 6 or higher.
For example, as a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots (one level 2 slot or two level 1 slots).
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

2.name: Scholar
2.notes: In addition to your magical studies, you specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion. You gain Expertise in the chosen skill.

3.name: Divination Savant
3.notes:
Add two free level 1–2 Divination Wizard spells to your spellbook.
Whenever you gain a new level of spell slots, add one free Divination spell of a level you can cast.

3.name: Portent
3.notes:
After each Long Rest, roll two d20s and record the results.
You may replace any D20 Test (yours or a creature you can see) with one of these rolls, chosen before the roll.
Each foretelling roll can be used once; unused rolls vanish when you finish a Long Rest.
You may replace only one roll per turn.

traits.name: Otherworldly Presence
traits.notes: You know the Thaumaturgy cantrip. When you cast it with this trait, the spell uses the same spellcasting ability you use for your Fiendish Legacy Trait.

traits.name: Fiendish Legacy
traits.notes: You are the recipient of a legacy that grants you supernatural abilities. Choose a legacy from the Fiendish Legacies table. You gain the level 1 benefit of the chosen legacy. When you reach character levels 3 and 5, you learn a higher-level spell, as shown on the table. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for the spells you cast with this trait (choose the ability when you select the legacy).

subrace.name: Abyssal
subrace.notes: Level1: - You have Resistance to Poison damage. You also know the Poison Spray cantrip. Level3: - Ray of Sickness. Level5: - Hold Person

feats.notes: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.
feats.name: Skilled

feats.notes: Push. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals Bludgeoning damage, you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space if the target is no more than one size larger than you.Enhanced Critical. When you score a Critical Hit that deals Bludgeoning damage to a creature, attack rolls against that creature have Advantage until the start of your next turn.
